title: Galen and the Silver Mould
markdown:
Galen’s fingers trembled, not with warm soil, but with cold dread. Silver mould crawled the Grand Greenhouse wall, devouring labels, each lost word a memory gone. Whisp, his vacuum-proof microbot, buzzed, blue lights fixed on the creeping ruin. This was not dust. It was eating his ordered world.

“It is consuming everything,” he whispered. Sunpetals were next. He had until sundown.

The Whispering Caves’ entrance gaped, exhaling cool damp air and wet stone. Shadows danced. Water dripped into whispers. “Are we right, Whisp?” His voice was a thread. A rock skittered ahead. The crack amplified his terror. He froze, picturing himself lost.

Whisp nudged his hand, a small blue beacon. Galen breathed and followed. Echoes twisted, mimicking doubt, almost turning him back. Then a faint warm luminescence bloomed ahead.

A crystal pulsed in a hidden cavern. Between them and it lay pale dusty spores. Galen knew they were sneaky. Some would cling to Whisp. He hesitated, hand hovering. He saw the glint of dust on Whisp’s antenna. He took the breath anyway. Fingers brushed the cool surface. A puff of ancient dust erupted. A single shimmering spore settled on Whisp’s primary sensor. Galen flinched. Whisp’s lights flickered. The hum became desperate clicks. A chill swept the cavern. That was the price.

Crystal in hand, they emerged into sunlight. Back in the greenhouse he set it on a pedestal. A soft hum filled the air. The silver mould recoiled, shriveling, labels clear. Order returned to the wall.

The next morning a speck of mould sat on his workbench. Galen’s breath hitched, a shadow of the old fear. Then he saw Whisp already investigating, lights blinking curiosity. He knelt. “Let us see what we can learn.” The mould glinted, no longer a threat, a small mystery with a name he had not given it yet.
characters: Galen (an apprentice gardener), Whisp (a vacuum-proof microbot)
